source_text: Ἡμεῖς δὲ καὶ εἱμαρμένης ἐσμὲν ἀνώτεροι, καὶ ἀντὶ πλανητῶν δαιμόνων ἕνα τὸν ἀπλανῆ δεσπότην μεμαθήκαμεν, καὶ οὐ καθ’ εἱμαρμένην ἀγόμενοι τοὺς ταύτης νομοθέτας παρῃτήμεθα.
pass_a_gloss: But we are also above fate, and instead of wandering demons we have learned one unwandering Master, and not being led according to fate we have rejected its lawgivers.
pass_b_english: But we ourselves stand above fate. Instead of wandering demons we have learned one Master who does not wander, and since we are not driven by fate we have refused the ones who wrote its laws.

choices.why: Pun against planetary demons; keep the wordplay.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly render the contrast between 'wandering demons' (πλανητῶν δαιμόνων) and the 'unwandering Master' (ἀπλανῆ δεσπότην). The translation of 'τοὺς ταύτης νομοθέτας' as 'its lawgivers' (Pass A) and 'the ones who wrote its laws' (Pass B) both preserve the sense of the Greek. The agency and negation are correctly maintained.
